review.scope: Seventeen exact defect/control pairs across twelve synthetic and five pinned public repository groups. ARC001: a three-layer Python package whose route layer imports the model layer directly. One Python architecture case stays unsupported_syntax (dynamic import, no paired defect) and is excluded from accuracy ratios. PSR005 (spec 094): a Spec Kit-installed skill edited after install, or left intact beside an edited authored skill; the evaluation pair is a separate group. PSR006 (spec 099): a monorepo with a scaffolder template AGENTS.md below templates/<app>/files/ (defect) and without it (control). STR004 (spec 100): a package AGENTS.md that pushes its chain over a 200 byte budget (defect), and a scaffolder template AGENTS.md the budget does not count (control).
review.methodology: Labels were authored from pinned source and seeded mutations before DocGuard output was reviewed. The ARC001 pair (2026-09-18), the PSR005 pairs (2026-11-12), the PSR006 pair and the STR004 pair (2026-11-13) were authored labels-first and matched their labels on the first run, except that the PSR005 evaluation pair first abstained until an early return in Path-Scoped-Rules was fixed. The STR004 control fails on the code before spec 100, where the template chain was counted.
review.limitations: Finite scoped cases do not establish exhaustive documentation or detector correctness. Ten of the tool’s finding codes are measured here; the rest carry no benchmark evidence. ARC001, PSR006 and STR004 are each measured by a single defect/control pair in one repository group, so each point estimate is below the reporting floor and backs off to the whole-corpus tier.
review.caveat: Benchmark precision on a deliberately balanced corpus of 17 defect and 17 clean-control cases across 17 repository groups and 17 causal families. This is DocGuard's precision on labelled cases, not the probability that a finding in your repository is real; quote every ratio with its n and Wilson 95% bound.
